summary.text: 谁 means “who?” or “whom?” Its traditional counterpart 誰 combines speech-related 言 with 隹, assigned a sound role in the traditional analysis; the proposed ancient sound connection remains uncertain.

formation.text: The traditional graph 誰 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 言 contributes speech-related meaning and 隹 supplies a sound cue. The simplified graph 谁 is identified as the standardized counterpart of 誰, with 訁 simplified to 讠. The proposed ancient connection between 隹 and the pronoun’s sound is not settled by the reconstructions alone.

components.text: 言 is identified as the speech-related semantic component in traditional 誰. The simplified counterpart uses its simplified side form 讠.

隹 is identified as the phonetic element in traditional 誰. A reported bronze inscription is read with bare 隹 for 誰, but its relationship to the graph with 言 and the ancient sound explanation remain unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The cited reconstructions and current readings allow comparison, but do not independently prove the ancient phonetic relation or establish the pronunciation of the proposed horse-name 騅.

sound.text: The Middle Chinese reconstructions are similar, supporting comparison but not by themselves proving the historical component role.
In this Old Chinese system, the reconstructions differ; the comparison alone does not prove the phonetic analysis.
The current Mandarin readings are zhuī for 隹 and shuí or shéi for 誰; modern similarity does not establish their ancient sound relation.

history.text: Traditional 誰 is reported in bronze inscriptions with 言 and 隹. One reported form has a distorted 言 element and is interpreted paleographically as 騅; another inscription is read with bare 隹 for 誰. These reports do not establish a complete sequence of graphic change.

One interpretation proposes that a bronze graph first meant a dark horse, 騅, and that the sign was later reused for the interrogative 誰 because the words may have sounded alike. The horse-name’s pronunciation is not established, so this proposed sound-based borrowing remains uncertain.
誰 is identified as the traditional form corresponding to simplified 谁, with 訁 → 讠. The cited evidence does not specify when or by what exact graphic steps 谁 was standardized.

uncertainties.text: The earliest dated use of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun, and the dates and provenance of the reported bronze forms, remain unresolved. The inspected entry lists no oracle-bone example; that does not prove none exists.
The proposed dark-horse origin and sound-based borrowing, and the relationship between bare 隹 and 言 plus 隹, remain uncertain.
Interrogative, assertive “anyone,” and rhetorical uses are recorded without dates, so their chronology and development are unresolved.
No verified character-specific historical glyph image is available for display in this entry to illustrate the reported bronze forms.

senses.text: The traditional gloss 何也 and cited examples support an interrogative use for a person. The earliest surviving witness is not dated in the cited accounts.
Dictionary entries record an assertive use meaning “anyone,” but do not date it or establish whether it developed from the interrogative sense.
A dictionary records a rhetorical use, but its example is undated and its development from another sense is not established.

limitations.text: The examples establish several uses but not their chronology or transitions, so no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 谁 means “who?” or “whom?” Its traditional counterpart 誰 is analyzed with speech-related 言 and a sound role for 隹, though the proposed ancient sound connection remains uncertain.

components.text: 言 contributes speech-related meaning in traditional 誰; its simplified counterpart is 讠 in 谁.
隹 is analyzed as a sound element in 誰; the proposed ancient sound connection is uncertain.

relationships.text: The traditional analysis assigns 隹 a sound role in 誰. Reported reading comparisons support comparison but do not independently prove the historical relation; a bronze inscription is also reported with bare 隹 read as 誰.
谁 is identified as the standardized simplified counterpart of 誰; the component notation identifies 訁 → 讠.
言 contributes speech-related meaning in the traditional analysis of 誰; the simplified counterpart uses 讠.
